36004064.content_html:
Vida Rucli – architect, curator, editor – tends ruins and commons, edits publications, convenes people and drafts projects where dwelling means committing and curating is placemaking. “There is no life that is not geographic” writes Ruth Wilson Gilmore. She chose her geography: the small border village of Topolò/Topolove, where she started a collective publishing project - Robida - that later became a spatial practice, a radio signal, a garden, an orchard and an infrastructure for collective life. She cares for and holds dear the blackberry–plant of the commons, clearings in the deep forest, reading poetic theory, effervescence of minds, tender militancy.

She lectured in different universities, collaborated with the festival Climate Care (Floating University, Berlin, 2023) and is a member of the international research group Ecologies of Care and of Floating University, Berlin. Since May 2025 she is guiding, in the role of president of the board, the Institute for Slovene Culture in San Pietro al Natisone/Špietar.

36004069.content_html:
Vida Rucli
takes care of Robida collective’s publications and programs.
She writes, edits and curates while living in Topolò/Topolove (IT).

images.title: vida_web_7.jpg
images.description:
"How can publishing formats and methods mirror a place? Is there a difference between publishing from a city or a rural environment? How do places enter publications –
beyond the usual formality of being mentioned in colophons? How can a publication be porous to a place? Can a site leak in it, beside being the content of the work? Can publishing – whose main goal is to be dispersed, distributed widely and circulating – be also situated, localised, grounded and site-informed?
The simplest question behind what we call situated publishing could be: what role does place have in publishing practices?" → From Situated Publishing, a text for the publication Publishing Anecdotes by Roman Karrer (summer 2024).

images.title: vida_web_10.jpg
images.description: "Robida is not a local magazine for many reasons: it does not report on facts and events of the area where it is created and it does not speak only to a local public who reads it to get information about the place. However it is still a representation of the cultural ferment of this borderland area of Italy and it always sparks the interest of the inhabitants of these valleys. Robida is maybe a situated magazine because its reason to be is deeply grounded in a specific context." → Editorial for Robida magazine 8 island (2022).

images.title: Vida_web_16
images.description_html:
It demands the affective labour of adjacency is a collective reading performance, part of Echos in den Hügeln festival at the Bibliothek Andreas Züst (14-15.11.2026). The sentence, borrowed from Tina Campt, sets the vibe and suggests the topic of the Sunday reading session. For our purpose the “it” of the title refers to practices of hosting and reading, which both imply, in different ways, intimacy and proximity. Stemming from the research done during my residency at the Bibliothek in 2022 about comp(h)osting, fertile accumulations and residency aftercare, the reading will explore hospitality, intertextual intimacy and correspondence. 

The reading will be broadcasted on Radio Robida and narrowcasted via FM in other rooms of Alpenhof.

(Image: Rut Himmelsbach, Bibliothek Andreas Züst catalogue n.: KAEH 012)

images.title: Vida_web_17
images.description:
In origine le montagne avevano grandi ali. Volavano per il cielo e si fermavano sulla terra, seguendo il loro piacere. Allora la terra tremava e vacillava. Indra recise le ali alle montagne. Fissò le montagne alla terra per renderla stabile. Le ali diventarono nubi. Da allora le nubi si raccolgono intorno alle cime. (Roberto Calasso, La rovina di Kasch)

(Image: Williams, Emmett,
An Anthology of Concrete Poetry, Bibliothek Andreas Züst catalogue n.: KAH 012)
